message:
docs(policy): publishing is part of done, and the boundary is the account

User instruction, 2026-09-10: only what the gnlink account cannot do goes to the
NAS session; write a deployment script; from now on a version that is bumped,
built and published is DONE, and what follows is "waiting on the field test".

What changes is where done sits. It used to end at a handoff document, with the
publish belonging to someone else. It now ends after the publish and its external
verification, and "waiting on the field test" is a separate state rather than an
asterisk on completion.

What does not change, said explicitly because both are easy to read into it:

  - "Automatic deployment" is not "publish unreviewed code that compiles". The
    verifier's explicit OK is still a gate. What is gone is waiting for approval
    a second time, after that gate, purely to publish.
  - It is not permission to git push. Deployment here means publishing to the
    NAS. The standing hold on push outranks any tool or skill guidance.

The boundary is drawn by account permission rather than by habit: what gnlink
owns is done here, and only what it cannot do -- nginx, systemd, env, ACLs,
packages -- is handed over, with the concrete operations, the failure evidence
and a rollback attached.

The "릴리스 배포 계정 (NAS)" section was written by the verifier under direct user
instruction; it is extended here rather than duplicated, and committed here
because the verifier does not commit tracked files.
